findings.title: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential lookup fails, the handler does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC handlers elsewhere in the codebase throw `TRPCError` with an explicit code (e.g. NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) so the client can distinguish error types and so tRPC doesn't log/report it as an unexpected internal error. A plain `Error` will be surfaced to tRPC as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, meaning routine 'wrong credentialId / not owner' cases get logged/alerted as server errors and the client-side `onError` handler (which just shows a generic toast) can't differentiate an authorization failure from any other failure.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in its `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` with no query invalidation of its own. Since `cacheUpdatedAt` (which drives the 'Cache Status' section and whether it is shown at all) comes from the `connectedCalendars` query, after a successful cache deletion the dropdown will keep showing the stale 'Last updated' timestamp and the cache section won't disappear unless the external `onChanged` callback happens to invalidate exactly that query. This is inconsistent with the disconnect flow and can leave the UI showing outdated cache information right after the user is told 'Cache deleted successfully'.

findings.title: Cache status lookup bypasses the CalendarCache factory/feature-flag abstraction
findings.body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the pattern used elsewhere in this same PR (e.g. `CalendarService.ts`) to decide between the real repository and the mock based on whether calendar caching is enabled. Bypassing that abstraction means every call to the `connectedCalendars` query (used on every visit to calendar settings pages) now issues an additional `groupBy` query against the CalendarCache table even for users/teams for which calendar caching is disabled, and it diverges from the established DI pattern used by the rest of the cache feature.

findings.title: Unconditional bulk SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update appears unused by the new feature
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` on every invocation (which runs per Google webhook ping / sync), issuing a write against every SelectedCalendar row for the credential just to bump `updatedAt`. The PR's own notes state the frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`, not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, and explicitly ask whether this update should be removed. As shipped, this adds unnecessary database write load on a hot path with no consumer of the resulting value.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars type now requires fields not guaranteed by all producers
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` were widened from `Pick<SelectedCalendar, "externalId" | "integration" | "eventTypeId">` to also require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Only one producer of this shape (`UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts`) was updated in this PR to select those extra fields, and neither field is actually consumed anywhere in this file's logic (the new cache-status feature reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCacheRepository`, not from these fields). Any other caller in the codebase that builds a `UserWithCalendars`-shaped object without selecting `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` will fail to type-check against this widened contract, for no functional benefit tied to this feature.

findings.title: No automated tests for the new data-deleting deleteCache mutation
findings.body: The new `deleteCacheHandler` (and the related `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` repository method and mock) ship with no unit or integration tests, despite this being a mutation that deletes user data (calendar cache rows) based on an access-control check. The PR's own review checklist flags 'Confirm repository pattern correctness' and credential-access validation as untested high-priority items; without tests, a regression in the ownership check (`credential.userId === user.id`) or in the deletion scope could silently allow deleting another user's cache or fail to delete the intended one.

findings.title: Ownership check fetches the full Credential row including secret key material
findings.body: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` is called without a `select`, so it loads every column of the Credential row — including the `key` field, which stores the (encrypted) OAuth tokens/secrets — purely to verify that the credential exists and belongs to the user. This is unnecessary exposure of sensitive data in application memory/logs; the check should use `select: { id: true }` (or similar) to avoid pulling credential secrets into memory when they are never used.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted via `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`, ignoring the user's actual locale even though the component already imports and uses `useLocale()` for translations. Non-English users will see dates/times formatted in US English conventions while the rest of the UI (including this same dropdown's strings) is localized, which is an inconsistent and incomplete localization of the new feature.

findings.title: dev:cron now invokes `npx tsx` without tsx being a declared dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` does not appear anywhere in this package's `dependencies` or `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` remains, still used by other scripts). Using `npx` for a package that isn't pinned in the manifest means the command will fetch whatever version of `tsx` is available on the registry (or fail without network access), which is a reproducibility/supply-chain concern and is unrelated to this PR's calendar-cache feature.

findings.title: Leftover auto-generated warning comment contradicts the actual migration
findings.body: The migration's header comment states 'Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' immediately followed by SQL that adds the column WITH a `DEFAULT NOW()` specifically to handle non-empty tables. This is leftover boilerplate from Prisma's migration generator that was not cleaned up and is misleading/contradictory to anyone reading the migration history to understand why a default was used.

findings.title: sed syntax is macOS-only and will fail on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses BSD sed's syntax (`-i ''`), which is required on macOS but is invalid on GNU sed used by most Linux distributions/CI images (GNU sed would try to treat the empty string as the input file). Since this script is added to the shared `scripts/` directory for contributors to use, it will error out for any Linux-based developer who tries to run it to update `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`.
